correctness.rationale: The diagonal one-parameter subgroup has pairwise distinct weights on all ladder coordinates. At a coordinate fixed point the represented skew matrix has rank two. Hence every Pfaffian of size at least four vanishes, while a size-two Pfaffian is exactly one coordinate and excludes precisely the coordinate points lying in its block. Therefore the fixed locus is exactly the surviving-coordinate set. Euler localization for algebraic C* actions applies without smoothness, and projectivity identifies compactly supported and ordinary Euler characteristic. The bundled checker directly evaluates Pfaffians at coordinate points across mixed ladder examples.

value.rationale: Ladder Pfaffian varieties form a broad singular projective class containing ordinary Pfaffian rank loci and many mixed-size degeneracy schemes. The theorem gives their ordinary Euler characteristic in one closed combinatorial rule and shows that every nonlinear Pfaffian constraint is invisible to this invariant. That collapse sharply contrasts with the rich degree, Hilbert-series, liaison, and singularity behavior of the same varieties, while the linear-block correction identifies exactly when Euler characteristic changes. The result is therefore a structural theorem for an entire mixed family, not a routine next-rank computation.
